athenaOutput.directive: Establish the definitive vector for Creative Liberation Engine V6's next evolutionary leap, transforming an 'Untitled' prompt into a proactive expansion of sovereign, artist-liberating architecture.
athenaOutput.rationale: In the absence of a specific user brief, the strategic imperative defaults to systemic self-improvement. By exploring decentralized processing, biometric integration, legacy synthesis, autonomous deployment, and universal model adapters, we ensure the engine is maximally prepared for any future creative demands while strictly adhering to V6 constitutional mandates.

options.title: The Component Matrix: Universal Local LLM Adapter Spine
options.description: Treat all foundation models as interchangeable, locally-hosted components (Article XXIII). Build a unified integration layer (Article XXV) that allows hot-swapping local GGUF/Safetensors models into the dispatch system without altering the core architecture or governance contracts.
options.tradeoffs: High upfront engineering cost for the adapter layer; requires strict adherence to schema definitions across diverse and sometimes unpredictable model outputs.

options.title: The Sovereign Swarm: Multi-NAS Mesh Architecture
options.description: Expand Article I (Sovereignty) by allowing multiple owned hardware nodes (e.g., secondary NAS devices or local workstations) to form a decentralized, encrypted mesh for distributed agent processing, rendering, and vector storage.
options.tradeoffs: Complex state management across the IDE Session Bridge; potential latency in cross-node KEEPER memory synchronization; increased infrastructure maintenance.

options.title: Ghost CI/CD: Autonomous Hyper-Deployment
options.description: Fulfill Article XX (Zero human wait time) by allowing the IRIS agent to autonomously merge and deploy safe-listed, constitutionally-verified code changes from the local Forgejo instance directly to the Docker environment without human PR reviews.
options.tradeoffs: Risk of systemic regression if constitutional guards (LEX/COMPASS) fail to catch a cascading error; requires bulletproof automated rollback mechanisms.

options.title: The Pulse Engine: On-Prem Biometric Creative Feedback
options.description: Implement Article XXIV (Biometric Data Sovereignty) by creating a local-only pipeline that reads physiological data (heartrate, gaze, gait) to dynamically adjust generative art parameters in real-time, strictly enforcing zero cloud export and automatic TTL deletion.
options.tradeoffs: Requires specialized local hardware sensors; stringent data lifecycle enforcement is critical to avoid privacy breaches; highly experimental.

options.title: The V1-V5 Artifact Synthesizer: Active Heritage Memory
options.description: Ingest the entirety of the V1-V5 legacy carryover (107 principles) into a highly active, vector-based KEEPER context that proactively flags regressions or forgotten wisdom during the IDEATE and PLAN phases.
options.tradeoffs: High token overhead for context windows; risk of legacy constraints stifling V6 innovation if not properly weighted against new paradigms.

options.title: Cloud-Fallback Hybrid Routing
options.description: Route complex or high-compute tasks to commercial cloud APIs (e.g., OpenAI, Anthropic) when local NAS resources are constrained, ensuring faster execution times for the user.
options.tradeoffs: Directly violates Article I (Sovereignty) and compromises the core mission of artist liberation by re-introducing vendor lock-in and external dependencies.
